title: Oi!
label: Go! Beat
format: CD single (catalogue number as listed by the Official Charts Company); Wikipedia notes a promo issue in 2001 but gives no format for it

type.basis: Charted at no. 8 in March 2002 and widely called the first grime song in the UK chart, but sources also tag it UK garage. Kept in the type series as a transitional specimen; whether it outranks Pulse X on priority is a question for the panel.

sound.text: Wikipedia describes heavy bass together with numerous UK garage-style elements, and lists the record as both grime and garage.
A 20th-anniversary retrospective notes stop-start rhythms, quick-fire quotable lines and punchy energy, and places the track in the moment when garage was 'darkened and twisted' into grime.

context.text: Peaked at no. 8 on the Official Singles Chart (first chart date 16/03/2002, 8 weeks) and no. 2 on the Official Dance Singles Chart.
Wikipedia's More Fire Crew article calls it widely recognised as the first grime song to reach the UK Singles Chart.
More Fire Crew (Lethal Bizzle, Ozzie B, Neeko) are from Waltham Forest, London, and built their profile hosting a show on the pirate station Deja Vu FM.
The video received heavy rotation on Channel U in 2003 and became one of its most requested videos.
Stereogum (2016) calls it 'the inaugural grime anthem'.

rels.other: Lethal Bizzle - Pow! (Forward) (2004): solo single by a More Fire Crew member, with Ozzie B and Neeko also featured

uncertainty: Genre labelling differs: the song's Wikipedia page lists it as grime and garage, the More Fire Crew article and Stereogum call it grime, and the Trench retrospective places it in the transition from garage to grime. Wikipedia says a promo was issued in 2001; no promo format or catalogue number was verified. The label is styled 'Go Beat' by the OCC and on the song page, and 'Go! Beat' on the crew page. Discogs could not be fetched.
tracklist: Wikipedia says the CD single included the music video. The track also appears on the crew's debut album More Fire Crew C.V. (Go! Beat, 27 January 2003).

audit.note: Song-page genre read from Apple's meta keywords (no visible genre line on song pages). Credited to Lethal Bizzle, not Platinum 45; page date 27 Jan 2003. Many DJ-mix versions also exist.
